exposure: gestational particulate air pollution (black carbon, PM2.5)
cohort: The study evaluated 1484 mother-child pairs participating in the ENVIRONAGE cohort, which includes mothers giving birth at the East-Limburg hospital in Genk, Belgium, who did not have planned caesarean sections and could fill out a Dutch questionnaire.
finding: Gestational exposure to particulate air pollution (black carbon and fine particulate matter) was associated with increased cord blood cystatin C levels, indicating an effect on newborn kidney function, with the strongest associations observed from week 27 onwards.
